 ATP Stockholm Day 3 Predictions Including Lorenzo Musetti vs Toby Samuel 
 Share Share this article
 × X Facebook LinkedIn WhatsApp Reddit Email Copy 
 The final tournament of 2026 awaits dozens of ATP stars this week in Stockholm, as the 20 remaining players will want to end the season on a high note. LWOT predicts Tuesday’s matchups at the ATP 250 event.   
 ATP Stockholm Day 3 Predictions 
 Tomas Martín Etcheverry vs Thiago Agustín Tirante 
 Head-to-head: First meeting 
 Etcheverry struggled on Monday against the home Swede Max Dahlin. Despite landing 85% of his first serves and not dropping serve, a 6-4 6-7 6) 6-3 victory might have taken more out of him than he expected. Tirante took out the more seasoned Jaume Munar in his Stockholm opener, in straight sets. This should be a fun all-Argentine clash, but unlike Etcheverry, Tirante holds a stronger win-rate on hard courts and upset Novak Djokovic earlier this season in Cincinnati . Etcheverry suffered a tough six-match losing streak earlier in the fall, only ending last week at the ATP 1000 in Paris.
 Prediction: Tirante in 3  
 Quentin Halys vs Lorenzo Sonego 
 Head-to-head: 1-1  
 As Halys will look to dictate this match with his big serve, Sonego already has two matches behind him as a qualifier. The Italian has struggled for much of 2026, and his ranking has tumbled to No. 115, his lowest since 2019 . Sonego similarly likes to play first-strike tennis, but the Frenchman enjoyed more success throughout 2026, winning a first ATP Tour title and recently hoisting a doubles trophy at the Paris Masters event . Sonego does have six wins at this ATP 250 event throughout his career, compared to Halys’ one.
 Prediction: Halys in 2 
 Aug 6, 2022; Montreal, Quebec, Canada; Quentin Halys (FRA) shows pride after socring a point against Ricardas Berankis (LTU) (not pictured) in first round qualifying play at IGA Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Kirouac-USA TODAY Sports 
 Lorenzo Musetti vs Toby Samuel  
 Head-to-head: First meeting 
 After qualifying for the main draw, Samuel dominated home wild card Leo Borg in a 6-3 6-2 rout; it was a tough showing from Bjorn Borg’s son, after he had reached the second round in Stockholm last year and nearly upset the No. 3 seed. Samuel, at No. 95 in the world, continues to cement himself as a likely spot in the Australian Open main draw, and a big week in Stockholm should secure that.
 Injuries derailed much of Musetti’s season , but he’s enjoyed a strong finish to the year, winning the ATP 250 title in Lyon in October, and upsetting World No. 1 Alexander Zverev in Paris last week. The Italian should be too solid here.
 Prediction: Musetti in 2
